{{one source |date=May 2024}}
A '''Kharitonov region''' is a concept in [[mathematics]]. It arises in the study of the [[Stable polynomial|stability of polynomials]].

Let <math>D</math> be a [[simply-connected set]] in the [[complex plane]] and let <math>P</math> be the polynomial family.

<math>D</math> is said to be a '''Kharitonov region''' if

:<math>V_T^n(V_S^n)</math>

is a subset of <math>P.</math> Here, <math>V_T^n</math> denotes the set of all [[vertex polynomial]]s of complex interval polynomials <math>(T^n)</math> and <math>V_S^n</math> denotes the set of all vertex polynomials of real interval polynomials <math>(S^n).</math>
